vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: duhui-all-to-pdf
Version: 1.0.3

The skill facilitates document-to-PDF conversion via the Duhui API on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace. The script (scripts/duhui_doc_to_pdf.py) implements a transparent workflow: fetching temporary OSS credentials from the vendor, uploading the local source file to a temporary Alibaba OSS bucket, and calling the conversion API. The SKILL.md instructions provide clear guidance for the agent to handle missing API keys (DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE) securely without echoing them, and the overall behavior is strictly aligned with the stated purpose of the tool.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality and network calls match its description, but it explicitly instructs the agent to solicit and accept a sensitive AppCode through the chat and uploads local files to vendor-controlled OSS — both privacy-sensitive behaviors that deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (convert local documents to PDF via Duhui async API) align with the required binary (python3), the single env var (DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE), and the code which uploads a single local file to OSS then calls convert_async and polls for results.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly encourages the agent to prompt users to paste DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE into the chat and states the agent will inject it into the execution environment. This directs acquisition of a secret via the conversational channel and gives the agent instructions about injecting/storing it — a risky practice. The instructions also mandate uploading the user's local file to a vendor-controlled OSS bucket and sending its URL to the vendor; that is data exfiltration by design (expected for this service) but must be surfaced to users.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with a small Python script and no install spec. No external packages are installed; required binary is only python3. No downloads from untrusted hosts during install.

dimensions.detail: Only DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE is required, which is proportionate to calling Alibaba's AppCode-protected API. However, the runtime also fetches temporary OSS credentials from a vendor URL (https://file.duhuitech.com/k/tmp_up.json) to upload files — this is expected for the workflow but means the skill obtains and uses temporary credentials at runtime and will place user files on a vendor-controlled OSS bucket.

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do exactly what it claims (upload a single local file to the vendor's OSS and call Duhui's async convert API), but it has two important privacy/security implications:

- Secret handling: The skill instructs the agent to ask users to paste DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE into the chat and then inject it into the execution environment. Do NOT paste sensitive credentials into chat unless you understand and accept that chat logs (or other systems) may persist them. Prefer injecting the AppCode via a secure secret store or the agent's secret-injection mechanism rather than sending it in an open conversation.

- Data exfiltration: Your local file will be uploaded to a vendor-controlled OSS bucket (fmtmp.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com) and processed on the vendor side. Do not use this skill for documents you cannot share with the vendor (sensitive PII, secrets, regulatory data) unless you have explicit authorization and have reviewed the vendor's privacy/security terms.

Before installing or invoking:
- Consider using a local converter (LibreOffice, wkhtmltopdf, etc.) for sensitive documents.
- If you must use this skill, inject AppCode via a secure secret store or environment injection mechanism (not plain chat). Verify retention and deletion guarantees with the vendor.
- Be aware the script attempts to delete the temporary OSS object but deletion is best-effort and may fail, leaving a short-lived copy on vendor storage.
